description: Bromine is a chemical element with symbol Br and atomic number 35. It is a volatile red-brown liquid at room temperature that evaporates readily to form a similarly colored vapor. Its properties are intermediate between those of chlorine and iodine, and it is one of only two elements that is liquid at standard temperature and pressure.
uses: Bromine is used as a fire retardant, with more than half the bromine produced worldwide annually serving this purpose. Bromine compounds are also used in well drilling fluids, photographic film, and as intermediates in the manufacture of organic chemicals, as well as having pharmaceutical applications such as antiepileptics.
characteristics: Bromine is a very reactive nonmetal that freezes at −7.2 °C and boils at 58.8 °C. It has a very penetrating, choking, and unpleasant odor derived from the Greek word for stench, and its color results from specific electron transitions between molecular orbitals, appearing pale yellow when solid but reddish-brown as a liquid.
